glosses: To remain in a particular place, especially for a definite or short period of time; sojourn; abide.

examples.text: We stayed in Hawaii for a week.  I can only stay for an hour.

She would commaund the hasty Sunne to stay,
Or backward turne his course from heuen's hight,
Stay, I command you; stay and hear me first,

1874 Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, “Three Friends of Mine,” IV, in The Masque of Pandora and Other Poems, Boston: James R. Osgood, 1875, p. 353,
I stay a little longer, as one stays / To cover up the embers that still burn.
“Well,” I says, “I cal'late a body could get used to Tophet if he stayed there long enough.” ¶ She flared up; the least mite of a slam at Doctor Wool was enough to set her going.

glosses: To continue to have a particular quality.

examples.text: Wear gloves so your hands stay warm.
Promise me you'll always stay/remain my little prince.
For as the Flames augment, and as they stay / At their full Height, then languish to decay, / They rise, and sink by Fits […]

The three men in the room stayed motionless, holding their breaths.

The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you "stay up to date with what your friends are doing",[…]and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.

glosses: To prop; support; sustain; hold up; steady.

examples.text:
Lord Mayor of London. See, where he stands between two clergymen!
Duke of Buckingham. Two props of virtue for a Christian prince,
To stay him from the fall of vanity:

But Moses hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
Draw in your right elbow, turn your hand outward and bear it lightly, gripe not the pen too hard, with your left hand stay the paper.

Sallows and Reeds, on Banks of Rivers born,
Remain to cut; for Vineyards useful found,
To stay thy Vines and fence thy fruitful Ground.

glosses: To support from sinking; to sustain with strength; to satisfy in part or for the time.

examples.text: […] he has devoured a whole loaf of bread and butter, as fast as Phoebe could cut it, and it has not staid his stomach for a minute […]

glosses: To stop or delay something.
To stop; detain; keep back; delay; hinder.

examples.text: Your ships are stay’d at Venice.

1671, John Evelyn, Diary, entry dated 14 November, 1671, in The Diary of John Evelyn, London: Macmillan, 1906, Volume 2, p. 337,
This business staid me in London almost a week […]
[…] I was willing to stay my Reader on an Argument, that appears to me new […]

The task of recalling him from the vagrancy into which he always sank when he had spoken, was like recalling some very weak person from a swoon, or endeavouring, in the hope of some disclosure, to stay the spirit of a fast-dying man.

[…] she filled the room she entered, and felt often as she stood hesitating one moment on the threshold of her drawing-room, an exquisite suspense, such as might stay a diver before plunging while the sea darkens and brightens beneath him […]
She rose to leave but Libor stayed her.

glosses: To stop or delay something.
To restrain; withhold; check; stop.

examples.text:
1597, Richard Hooker, Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity, Book 5, in The Works of Mr. Richard Hooker, London: Andrew Crook, 1666, p. ,
[…] all that may but with any the least shew of possibility stay their mindes from thinking that true, which they heartily wish were false, but cannot think it so […]
So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul.

1852, Charlotte Brontë, letter cited in Elizabeth Gaskell, The Life of Charlotte Brontë, 1857, Volume 2, Chapter 10,
[…] you must follow the impulse of your own inspiration. If THAT commands the slaying of the victim, no bystander has a right to put out his hand to stay the sacrificial knife: but I hold you a stern priestess in these matters.

Between Pegāna and the Earth flutter ten thousand thousand prayers that beat their wings against the face of Death, and never for one of them hath the hand of the Striker been stayed, nor yet have tarried the feet of the Relentless One.

glosses: To stop or delay something.
To cause to cease; to put an end to.

examples.text: Now stay your strife […]

glosses: To stop or delay something.
To put off; defer; postpone; delay; keep back.

examples.text: The governor stayed the execution until the appeal could be heard.

glosses: To hold the attention of.
To bear up under; to endure; to hold out against; to resist.

examples.text:
She will not stay the siege of loving terms,
Nor bide the encounter of assailing eyes,

glosses: To wait for; await.

examples.text: My father stays my coming;

glosses: To remain for the purpose of; to stay to take part in or be present at (a meal, ceremony etc.).

examples.text: I stay dinner there.

How glad they had been to hear papa invite him to stay dinner, how sorry when he said it was quite out of his power […]

glosses: To rest; depend; rely.

examples.text: Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon:

glosses: To stop; come to a stand or standstill.
To come to an end; cease.

examples.text: That day the storm stayed.
Here my commission stays,

glosses: To dwell; linger; tarry; wait.

examples.text: Yet not to be wholly silent of all your Charities I must stay a little on one Action, which preferr’d the Relief of Others, to the Consideration of your Self.

glosses: To make a stand; to stand firm.
To hold out, as in a race or contest; last or persevere to the end; to show staying power.

examples.text: That horse stays well.

glosses: To wait; rest in patience or expectation.

examples.text: I’ll tell thee all my whole device / When I am in my coach, which stays for us.

glosses: To wait as an attendant; give ceremonious or submissive attendance.

examples.text:

That stays upon me […]

glosses: To live; reside.

examples.text: Hey, where do you stay at?

glosses: Continuance or a period of time spent in a place; abode for an indefinite time.

examples.text: I hope you enjoyed your stay in Hawaii.

glosses: A postponement, especially of an execution or other punishment.

examples.text: The governor granted a stay of execution.

glosses: A stop; a halt; a break or cessation of action, motion, or progress.

examples.text: stand at a stay

glosses: A fixed state; fixedness; stability; permanence.

examples.text: The wisdom, stay, and moderation of the king.

glosses: Hindrance; let; check.

examples.text: They were able to read good authors without any stay, if the book were not false.

glosses: A prop; a support.

glosses: A piece of stiff material, such as plastic or whalebone, used to stiffen a piece of clothing.

examples.text: Where are the stays for my collar?

glosses: A corset.

examples.text: Her figure was tall, yet not too tall; comely and well-developed, yet not fat; her head set on her shoulders with an easy, pliant firmness; her waist, perfection in the eyes of a man, for it occupied its natural place, it filled out its natural circle, it was visibly and delightfully undeformed by stays.

examples.text: Souvent on entend parler d’un accident, —un étai a manqué, une corde s’est rompue, un homme a été écrasé.— À la surface de la terre on croit que c’est un malheur ; trente pieds au-dessous on sait que c’est un crime.

On disposa à l’intérieur des chambres des étais placés verticalement, qui multiplièrent les points d’appui aux poutres du plafond.
Je les compare, ces sentiments, à ces étais grâce auxquels on élève une arche, mais qu’on enlève après que la clef de voûte est posée.

examples.text: Au moyen de palans je « roidis » les étais et j’amarre le beaupré aussi solidement qu’il est possible sur le pont maintenant rasé à l’avant.

Étai. C’est à peu près la même chose que la draille, mais à cette différence que l’étai relie l’étrave (ou l’extrémité du bout-dehors) au sommet du grand mât. L’étai sert à tenir le mât et aussi à établir le foc, tourmentin, génois (voir dessin p. 49)

— […] il découvrit bientôt la carcasse de l’un des monoplans asiatiques […] La machine avait évidemment opéré une chute verticale et elle était demeurée à demi suspendue dans un groupe d’arbres […] ses ailes tordues et rompues, ses étais disjoints s’enchevêtraient dans les branchages fracassés, et la pointe avant était fichée dans le sol.

Voir la section « Chevronnel / étai » de l'article consacré par Wikipédia au chevron en héraldique, ainsi que la section « Étai » de l'article Liste de pièces héraldiques.
